$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for cross-process error codes. Every code names WHO produces it via `producer`: `rust` codes are assigned by the MCP server (src/error.rs, verified by the codes_match_contract test), `extension` codes travel on BridgeResp.code (extension/src/shared/bridge-error.ts, allowlisted in src/error.rs EXTENSION_CODES), and `reserved` codes are deliberately unimplemented with the reason stated. A code with no producer is a lie the clients act on -- `retryable` is per-code metadata, so an unproducible retryable code means transient failures get reported as permanent. The every_code_has_a_producer test fails if one appears.

errors.message: The tool arguments were missing or invalid.

The browser extension is not connected. Most often its MV3 service worker is asleep (Chrome stops it after ~30s idle) — the extension re-checks every 30s, so a retry usually succeeds; otherwise the user clicks the toolbar icon.
The extension and server protocol versions are incompatible; reload or upgrade the extension.
errors.reserved: The capability/version handshake that would emit this is deferred until there is a real protocol v2 to reject -- see contracts/capabilities.json handshake.onMismatch.

errors.message: The extension cannot act on the tab yet -- most often it was just opened and has not navigated, so it has no URL. Retry shortly.
This tool is disabled in the extension settings.
The target tab could not be found; it was closed or the id is stale. Call tab_list again.
The tool cannot run on this page (e.g. chrome://, the Web Store, or a DevTools-attached tab).
The extension executed the operation but it failed.
The message exceeded the native-messaging size limit.
errors.reserved: Nothing measures outbound frames against the 1MB native-messaging limit yet; exceeding it makes Chrome close the port instead. Kept because a guard is wanted (page_screenshot can plausibly exceed it), not because it is produced.

errors.message: The extension did not respond in time.
The bridge connection was lost while awaiting a response.
